text:
Anjali: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands — the pricing/credits segment got cut short. Opening this thread for any detailed Qs about quotas, exemptions, and SLA behavior. Drop product/ops questions here and we'll follow up.

Marcus: Thanks! Quick one — if a customer exhausts reserved credits during the month, do we auto-bill or throttle? Example: Dedicated customers with burst enabled.

Anjali: Short answer: we don't auto-bill for overage unless there's an explicit overage clause in the contract. Default behavior is graceful degrade to a lower-cost compatible model + an email/console notification. For Hosted free-tier customers we throttle. We'll add a UI/config knob for overage handling.

Devon: Where is that policy documented? I couldn't find it in billing docs.

Anjali: Docs PR is WIP — working link (placeholder): https://docs.redwood.ai/usage-policies. We'll add a decision flowchart and examples.

Priya: For quota exemptions (e.g., infra smoke tests, partner demos) — can teams request temporary exemptions? What's the approval SLA?

Marcus: +1 — need this for partner onboarding demos next week.

Ethan: Ops note — we already support short-term org whitelists by org-id for infra/partner demos. Submit a request in #infra-requests with the template. Current operational SLA is ~48h on business days; escalate for emergencies.

Marta: Is there a way to set per-route soft-limits? For some routes we want retries + cached responses and not have them eat into the main bucket.

Ken: Per-route soft-limits are on the roadmap for Q2. Right now you can do per-api-key rate caps and model routing policies. Soft-limits and per-route priorities will land as a Console feature.

Liam: Clarify credit expiry — do trial credits expire after 90 or 180 days? I've seen both referenced.

Anjali: Official policy: trial credits = 90 days. Promotional vouchers vary by campaign and have their own T&Cs. We're standardizing the messaging on the billing page this week.

Devon: Can we show an example header that the API returns so teams can read remaining quota in the SDK? Handy for frontend UX.

Marcus: SDKs already surface these. Example curl headers:

```
curl -I -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
# response headers include:
x-rw-credits-remaining: 4123
x-rw-quota-window-end: 2026-04-01T00:00:00Z
x-rw-rate-limit-remaining: 120
```

Priya: Who signs off on quota-exemption requests? CS or Revenue? Need to know for partner asks.

Anjali: CS triages standard whitelists. Any contractual changes (credit top-ups, billing adjustments) require Revenue approval. For one-off emergency whitelists CS + Oncall can OK and notify Revenue post-facto.

Ethan: One more — when we fallback to a smaller model as part of graceful degradation, do we have documented expectations (latency delta, quality caveats) that we can communicate to customers?

Ken: Good point. We're adding fallback metadata to the Console: expected latency delta, token-cost delta, and a short note on quality tradeoffs. Roadmap item owned by eng-platform.

Marcus: ETA on per-route soft-limits / pilot?

Ken: Targeting a closed pilot in ~6-8 weeks, public beta afterwards depending on pilot feedback.

Marta: Please add me to follow-up doc — want to capture partner edge cases and demo requirements.

Anjali: @Marta added. I'll consolidate these Qs and post action items here after I sync with Revenue and Eng.

OpsBot: Meeting recording uploaded: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01XXXXXX/p1912345678000000

Marcus: :thumbsup: Thanks everyone, this helps.
